title: Nagata and J-2 ascend together along weakly etale maps
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $f:A\to B$ be weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Assume $A$ is Nagata [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and J-2 [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Then $B$ is Nagata and J-2. Here J-2 means that in every finite type algebra over the ring the set of primes with regular local localization is open; this is the J-2 predicate explicitly defined in [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Mathematical Journal 60 (1976), 139–149, DOI 10.1017/S0027763000017190
source.place: Theorem 5.3(ii), printed pp. 146–147 (PDF pp. 8–9); Remark 5.2 for weakly etale = AF. The proof refers to Greco 1971, results 4.8, 2.9, 4.11. Definitions: Stacks Tag 032R (definition-nagata), Tag 07P7 (definition-J).

proof.text: Apply the finite normalization construction to each prime q of B and each finite extension of kappa(q). It gives D finite over B, integrally closed, with fraction field L, and an injective weakly etale map R->D from a domain R finite over A. For the Nagata clause, transport the canonical quotient fraction field to kappa(q). Since D is integral over B/q and normal with fraction field L, its elements are precisely the integral closure of B/q in L. More explicitly that integral closure embeds B-linearly into D, so it is finite over B and then over B/q. Every B/q is Japanese.

For each finite purely inseparable residue extension use the same D and R. J-2 for A makes the regular locus of R open, since a finite A-algebra is of finite type. Pull this locus back along Spec D->Spec R. It contains the zero prime because R->D is injective and the zero-prime localization of the domain R is a field, hence regular. It is thus a nonempty open.

All fibres of R->D are absolutely flat weakly etale field algebras. They are Noetherian, as quotients of localizations of D, and their prime localizations are fields, hence regular. For any q in the pulled-back open, localize the flat map at q and its contraction. Identify its closed fibre with the localization of the corresponding fibre ring via Ideal.Fiber.algEquivAux₂. Apply flat local regularity ascent to get regularity of D_q.

The finite models D have fraction field L and a nonempty regular open. Apply the residue-field criterion for J-2. Combine this conclusion with the Nagata clause. The case B=0 has no primes and is covered by the same quantified statements.

proof_origin.document: Stacks Project, Algebra and More on Algebra
proof_origin.place: The original finite normalization construction (steps 3–7) is proved in the new finite-residue-model lemma; Nagata follows by integral closedness, and J-2 by Tag 07PC and local regularity ascent Tag 031E on the inverse image of the regular locus. No principal-open localization is required.
